summary: Create a bound function object preserving bound this, leading arguments, length/name metadata, and target call/construct behavior.

target.notes: The helper must create a new bound function exotic object. On ordinary calls it prepends bound args; if constructable and invoked with new, bound this is ignored and the target is constructed.

caveats: Bound functions can still be constructable if their target is constructable.
Using a C# closure alone misses new/instanceof/prototype/name/length behavior.

tests.name: partial application
tests.input: function f(a,b){return this.x+a+b}; const g=f.bind({x:1},2); console.log(g(3));

tests.name: bound constructor ignores bound this
tests.input: function C(x){this.x=x}; const B=C.bind({bad:true},4); const o=new B(); console.log(o.x,o.bad);
